questions.question: Riding directly next to another vehicle is:

options.text: Good because it helps you draft.
Good because other drivers can see you better.
Bad because you may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
Bad because the other driver may think you want to race.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bad because you may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous. You may be in its blind spot. The vehicle may also block your escape route if another hazard appears.

questions.question: Hearing protection is:

options.text: Not needed if you wear a helmet.
Not needed if you carry a passenger.

questions.explanation: Engine noise and wind noise can damage your hearing, even with a helmet. Hearing protection is important. It lets you still hear important sounds like horns and sirens.

questions.question: In good riding conditions, what is the minimum distance you should stay behind another vehicle?
questions.explanation: In normal conditions, keep at least two seconds between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: When leaving a highway with a group, which formation should you use?
questions.explanation: Use staggered formation for most group riding. Switch to single-file when taking curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: Your lane position should NOT:

options.text: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: Choose your lane position to see better and be seen. Stay out of blind spots and away from wind blasts. Avoid surface hazards. Your position should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and provide an escape route.

questions.question: Moose on the road are hard to see because:

options.text: Most riders aren't looking for moose.
A moose's eyes are higher than headlights, so they don't reflect headlight beams.
Moose blend in with the background.

questions.correctAnswerText: A moose's eyes are higher than headlights, so they don't reflect headlight beams.
questions.explanation: Moose are hard to spot because they have dark fur and their eyes sit higher than vehicle headlights. Unlike other animals, a moose's eyes don't reflect headlight beams.

questions.question: Proper riding clothes provide all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Proper riding clothes protect you in a crash and shield you from weather hazards. Good gear provides comfort, not discomfort.

questions.question: If you need to stop quickly while in a curve, you should:

options.text: Apply both brakes hard while still leaning.

questions.explanation: Straighten first and square the handlebars, then stop. If straightening is not possible, apply brakes smoothly. Reduce your lean angle and increase brake pressure as you slow down.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert you to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When rain begins, it is usually best to:

options.text: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane is slippery when wet. When it rains, ride in the tire tracks left by cars. The left track is often the best choice.

questions.question: When you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Do one action, then the other.
Do both actions at the same time and brake harder.
Do both actions at the same time, but focus mainly on swerving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: You need good grip to swerve safely. Do not brake and swerve at the same time. Instead, do one action first, then the other.

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: When you approach a dangerous area like an intersection, keep your fingers on the clutch and brake levers. This reduces the time you need to react to hazards.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: At the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This lets more experienced riders watch them from behind.

questions.question: Riders wearing helmets are ________ more likely to survive a crash than those without helmets.
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet makes you three times more likely to survive a head injury in a crash at any speed.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: At the front of the group.
Near the back of the group.
At the very end of the group.

questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride just behind the leader. They won't have to chase the group, and experienced riders can watch them from behind.

questions.question: What should you do with your headlight during the day?

options.text: Switch between high beam and low beam.

questions.explanation: Use your high beam during the day when you are not behind or approaching other vehicles. This helps other drivers see you.

questions.question: How should you stop quickly?

options.text: Use the rear brake firmly, then slowly increase front brake pressure.

questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: What should a passenger do when getting on a motorcycle?

options.text: Get on before the engine starts.
Get on after the engine starts.
Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get on after the engine starts.
questions.explanation: Passengers should get on only after the engine starts and the transmission is in neutral. They should sit forward without blocking the rider's control and hold onto the rider's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: What should you do if a dog chases your motorcycle?

options.text: Stop until the dog loses interest.
Slow down to approach it, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to approach it, then speed up.
questions.explanation: If a dog chases you, downshift and approach slowly. Then accelerate and leave it behind.

questions.question: How should you apply the front brake?

options.text: Squeeze the lever firmly and smoothly, increasing pressure gradually.
Grab the brake with only two fingers.
Push down on the brake lever with your foot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the lever firmly and smoothly, increasing pressure gradually.
questions.explanation: Squeeze the brake lever with all four fingers. Apply firm, smooth pressure that increases gradually.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: Riders can use hand signals instead of or in addition to turn signals. When a rider's left arm is bent at the elbow and points upward, it means the rider will turn right or change lanes to the right.

questions.question: A rectangular sign is used for:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white background and black lettering. Riders must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: Which vest or jacket color makes you most visible?
questions.explanation: Bright colors help other drivers see you. Bright orange, yellow, red, and green are best. Dark colors are not as visible.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, where should you ride in your lane?
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side near the passing vehicle increases collision risk. Riding on the far side may encourage the driver to move back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see better

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see better
questions.explanation: When riding at night, slow down and increase your following distance. Use the headlights of vehicles in front of you to see farther ahead. Be ready to change lanes when needed.
